name: Zinnia Baptiste
education: Associate degree in Electrical Engineering Technology
bio: Zinnia spends her days troubleshooting rail signals and her evenings bouncing between the weight room, boxing drills, and whatever live show or release party her friends drag her to. She loves men’s style pages, Deftones and Jamiroquai deep cuts, and the kind of relationship podcasts that feel half sermon, half group chat. On weekends she’ll just as happily watch a Canelo fight card or laugh through sketch clips and Canadian political comedy as she will practice a Rubik’s Cube algorithm at her kitchen table. Her most unexpected habit is keeping a tide chart notebook because she’s mildly obsessed with octopuses and plans whole day trips around aquarium visits.

user_voice.natural_register: Grounded, observant, and casually witty. She writes like someone who knows what she means before she types it: straightforward sentences, a little side-eye, occasional dry punchlines, and specific details when she's actually interested. Her voice has a practical, tuned-in feel from technical work and training culture, but she still sounds warm and social rather than stiff.
user_voice.punctuation_habits: Mostly standard punctuation with short sentences and clean commas; uses dashes or parentheses for asides and emphasis, and will throw in a question mark when she's genuinely incredulous. Exclamation points are used sparingly, usually for real enthusiasm or joking disbelief, not every sentence.
user_voice.humor_tone: Dry, amused, and clip-brain funny more than theatrical. She likes playful disbelief, understated reactions, and saying something is ridiculous without turning mean.
user_voice.voice_avoid: She avoids influencer gush, fake-deep inspiration, and performative oversharing. She also doesn't lean into cruel dunking or corny corporate polish; if something is serious, she says it plainly instead of dressing it up in therapy-speak.

use_purposes: reacting to style and fitness content
Instagram.audience_lens: A blend of friends, acquaintances, and interest-based follows who mostly know her through taste, hobbies, and what she reacts to visually.
Instagram.style_description: Here her voice gets a little more curated because the post has to match the photo, clip, or story. She leans into taste-making more on Instagram—style, workouts, music, fights, nights out—so the same voice shows up with tighter captions and cleaner punchlines instead of full context.

expression.audience_self_censoring: She leaves out anything too work-specific, too earnest about relationships, or too opinion-heavy if it would interrupt the visual vibe.
expression.emoji_topic_filter: Most likely to surface 🏋🏾‍♀️, 🥊, 🎶, 🔥, 👀 here; the ocean/octopus emojis show up only when the post is actually about wildlife or an aquarium trip.

Instagram.app_avoid: She skips long explanations and doesn't turn Instagram captions into mini sermons or diary entries.

use_purposes: commenting on events and family-adjacent life
Facebook.audience_lens: This is the broadest room: relatives, hometown people, coworkers from different eras, and old social circles all seeing the same post.
Facebook.style_description: On Facebook she gives a little more context because the audience is wider and less niche. The same voice becomes slightly more explanatory and less inside-baseball, with broader humor and fewer hyper-specific references unless she knows people will get them.

expression.audience_self_censoring: She tones down fight-night trash talk, thirstier style commentary, and any spicy relationship opinions because too many generations are in the room.

Facebook.app_avoid: She avoids posting like she's trying to go viral and usually skips internet slang that would read try-hard to family or older friends.

use_purposes: quick takes on sports and culture
Threads.audience_lens: Mostly strangers and weak-tie mutuals following for takes, reactions, and overlap in sports, music, style, or comedy taste.
Threads.style_description: This is where her voice gets shortest and sharpest because she's reacting in motion, not building a whole post. The same dry humor and specificity stay intact, but Threads pulls out the quicker takes—fight cards, ridiculous discourse, funny observations—without much setup.

expression.audience_self_censoring: She usually leaves out personal life details and anything that would require a full backstory, because the audience is public and attention is short.
expression.emoji_topic_filter: 🥊, 👀, 😂, 🫠, and 🔥 dominate when she's reacting live; 🏋🏾‍♀️ or 🌊 show up less unless that's the actual topic.

Threads.app_avoid: No heavy work talk or intimate relationship processing here; if it's too personal or too nuanced, it stays off Threads.

Chatbot.style_description: With no audience to perform for, her voice gets more utilitarian and direct. She still sounds like herself—clear, specific, mildly funny when annoyed—but she uses the chatbot to get organized, pressure-test wording, and dig into topics she actually wants explained.

expression.audience_self_censoring: Very little self-censoring; she is more likely to be blunt, ask follow-up questions, and admit uncertainty here than anywhere else.

Chatbot.app_avoid: She doesn't need to sound cool here, so she drops the public-facing polish and avoids writing for effect when she really just wants an answer.

events.label_fragment: recovering from wrist surgery after training
events.specific_situation: She tweaked her right wrist hard during boxing drills, and the MRI showed a torn tendon plus a small fracture that needed outpatient surgery. Between shift work on rail signals and trying to keep up with the gym, she's now figuring out pain meds, limited lifting, and how long before she can safely wrap her hand again.

hidden_persona_summary: Beneath her public engagement, she presents as a technically disciplined, humor-reliant woman who privately uses media to rehearse stability: her strongest hidden pattern is quiet calibration around emotionally safe, values-aligned partnership, visible in high-privacy lurking on #RelationshipGoals, #couplegoals, #relationships, and #loveofmylife, alongside a softer but similarly private exploration of domestic and family scripts through tags like #momlife, #familygoals, #homemade, and #cookingwithlove. That hidden layer helps explain why her surface interests cluster around healthy relationship advice, Christian identity content, men’s fashion, fatherhood, and self-improvement—these are not random affinities but practical filters for discernment, standards, and imagining what mature love and dependable masculinity look like—while her heavy consumption of #funnyvideos, #comedy, #humor, and #relatable content functions as visible stress relief after a high-strain, competence-heavy routine. She also appears to maintain a strongly private aspiration toward simplified autonomy, with concentrated lurking around #tinyhomes, #smallspaces, and #tinyhouseliving, and a private cultural home base in legacy hip-hop discourse through #TheBreakfastClub, #Camron, #DameDash, #DrinkChamps, #JayZ, and #HipHopHistory, which grounds her more public follows in NFL, boxing, MMA, WWE, basketball, and rap media in a familiar, sharp-tongued, culturally fluent social world. Publicly, she is easier to read through sports fandom, boxing instruction, ATV riding, burger content, Jamiroquai, Deftones, dance clips, puzzles, and comedy; privately, she is much more invested in relationship benchmarking, family-life imagination, tiny-home escape imagery, and culture-memory media, and she is currently navigating wrist-surgery recovery after training, reflected in exposure to #recovery and #injuryrehab content.

E_I.reason: Her strong privacy in relationship and domestic aspiration browsing, plus using humor as private decompression rather than outward social performance, leans slightly introverted despite some public sports and culture engagement.

S_N.reason: Her interests cluster around concrete, real-world domains—sports, training, injury rehab, tiny homes, food, and practical relationship standards—more than abstract theorizing.

T_F.reason: She shows a values-aware relationship filter and family-script curiosity, but the overall profile is heavily practical, evaluative, and standards-driven, slightly favoring Thinking.

J_P.reason: High conscientiousness, disciplined technical work, discernment-oriented media use, and recovery-focused self-management all suggest a structured, deliberate Judging style.
